cover.title: Recoil Report — Jul 31 Tidio Call
cover.subtitle: Called expecting to pick a paid tier. Left having confirmed the current plan already does the job — lead delivery to SugarCRM needs no upgrade at all. Two-pass Recoil Protocol read (Deep Recall + Reverse Listening) against the Granola transcript.
cover.meta: Call: Jul 31, 2026 · 2:30 PM EDT · ~26 min · Zach Harris + Todd Hotes with D. Triana (Tidio, d.triana@tidio.net)
actions: Wire the flow's API call node

loadBearingQuote.text: We have one opportunity to keep the pricing lower than the 359 a month for sure... This can be done on your existing plan, even on this starter plan.
loadBearingQuote.attribution: D. Triana (Tidio rep) · Jul 31, 2026 — correcting the assumption live, screen-sharing the account

callWalk.label: Open
callWalk.title: Framed against overkill, not toward it
callWalk.body: Zach opens the account already upgraded once, then sets the real constraint before Daniel pitches anything: "I don't want to start with an overkill one just to be clear." That line, said before any plan was on the table, is what steered the whole call.

callWalk.label: Context
callWalk.title: Todd hands over the business model
callWalk.body: Todd explains PRL in full: raw resin pellets sold to injection molders who supply OEMs, formulations built per application (indoor/outdoor, electrical, medical). Customers often know the application, not the resin — PRL formulates. Grounds everything Daniel recommends afterward.

callWalk.label: Architecture
callWalk.title: Flow-first, AI-as-fallback confirmed
callWalk.body: Daniel walks the flow/AI split: flows are the deterministic lead-gen layer everyone hits first; Lyro AI (once enabled) is the conversational fallback for anyone who skips or exits a flow, and can keep qualifying ("are you interested in knowing more, or want to be contacted by a sales rep"). Copilot is a human-agent assist tool, distinct from full AI delegation.

callWalk.label: Pivot
callWalk.title: The tier question inverts
callWalk.body: Zach asks which tier unlocks the webhook. Daniel corrects the premise on screen: the flow's own "API call node" is a native webhook, live on the current plan — same for Zapier-from-flow. Only the AI acting on its own, pushing a lead out without a flow, needs the $359/mo Tidio+ tier. Real-time confusion on screen ("I think we're looking at the wrong page") resolves into the opposite of what the call was booked to decide.

callWalk.label: Close
callWalk.title: Downgrade, not upgrade
callWalk.body: Todd verbally approves dropping the wasteful Starter add-on (human-to-human ticketing, unneeded); Daniel prorates the $490/yr already paid and separately offers to chase a 5–10% account-wide discount for later. Admin access for Todd and the earlier email-DNS support ticket both handed off before the call ends.

signalThreads.label: REVERSAL
signalThreads.title: The call inverted its own premise
signalThreads.body: Booked to pick a paid tier. Left having confirmed no upgrade is needed for the one thing that actually mattered — lead delivery. The webhook everyone assumed was gated, wasn't.
signalThreads.note: Read backward from the close, this is the actual finding of the call, not a side note.

signalThreads.label: TRUST
signalThreads.title: The rep talked the account down, not up
signalThreads.body: Mid-call, unprompted: "I wouldn't recommend going for the growth plan... you can probably just skip this one." A vendor steering a customer toward less spend is a real signal, worth remembering the next time pricing comes up.

signalThreads.label: SCOPE
signalThreads.title: Flow vs AI is architecture, not upsell noise
signalThreads.body: The two-webhook split (flow-level vs AI-level) is a genuine product boundary in Tidio, confirmed on screen, not a sales tactic. Treat it as fact going forward, not as something to re-litigate.

signalThreads.label: OPEN LOOP
signalThreads.title: Two threads left genuinely open
signalThreads.body: BYO-LLM / MCP connection ("not sure, will get back to you") and the discount email ("early next week") are both unresolved. Neither blocks the build. Track them so they don't silently expire.

best.title: Wired and proven this week
best.body: The flow's API call node is connected to SugarCRM, one real test lead confirms it lands, and Daniel's discount email arrives on schedule for whenever Tidio+ becomes worth it.
best.note: Nothing here is blocked — this is just execution.

base.title: Wired now, discount lands whenever
base.body: Webhook wiring proceeds this week regardless of Daniel's follow-up. If the discount email is late or never comes, nothing changes — the current plan already does the job.
base.note: Most likely outcome; the discount was never load-bearing.

worst.title: The claim doesn't survive contact
worst.body: Something about the current plan's flow-level API action turns out to be capped or misconfigured once actually wired, contradicting what was shown on screen.
worst.note: Mitigation: send one real lead through before declaring this dependency closed. Don't take the screen-share as proof of production behavior.

riskFlags.label: Untested claim
riskFlags.body: Daniel's assurance that the API call node works on the current plan was confirmed verbally on a screen-share, not yet tested end-to-end with a live webhook firing into SugarCRM. Verify with one real lead before marking this dependency closed.

riskFlags.label: Discount is soft-committed
riskFlags.body: 5–10% offer contingent on manager approval, no firm date beyond "early next week." Not a blocker — track it so it doesn't quietly expire unacknowledged.

riskFlags.label: BYO-LLM / MCP genuinely unknown
riskFlags.body: Daniel could not answer whether PRL could bring its own LLM key or connect an MCP server; he is checking. Low priority — only matters if/when PRL wants to route Tidio through a different model directly.

riskFlags.label: No plan pressure
riskFlags.body: Unusually, the rep actively steered the account away from a bigger plan. Nothing here needs defensive negotiation on the next call.

protocol.label: Run 01
protocol.title: Wire the webhook this week
protocol.body: Use the flow's API call node (or Zapier-from-flow) to POST captured leads to SugarCRM on the current plan. Nothing left blocking this.

protocol.label: Run 02
protocol.title: Send one real test lead through
protocol.body: Confirms Daniel's claim holds in production, not just on his screen-share. Do this before closing the lead-delivery dependency in the build spec.

protocol.label: Run 03
protocol.title: Let the discount email arrive on its own
protocol.body: No chasing. If silent past roughly a week, one follow-up ping — not urgent, and doesn't block anything either way.

protocol.label: Close
protocol.title: Revisit Tidio+ only once ready to scale into AI qualification
protocol.body: Not before. The current plan is sufficient for everything Phase 1 needs.
